The downloader should accept these connection parameters from user configuration or reuse existing external-downloader settings instead of baking them into the implementation.

column5: Counting depth and stencil textures as color slots can send a framebuffer blit to the wrong attachment. The fix uses the actual color-attachment index.
column7: The draw-buffer target for each blit is chosen from `attachmentIndex`, which counts every attachment, not just color textures. If a destination framebuffer contains depth/stencil texture attachments before one or more color textures, `GL_COLOR_ATTACHMENT0 + attachmentIndex` will skip over the actual color slot and write to the wrong attachment. The read side uses `colorBufferIndex`, so the two sides can diverge. This should use a dedicated color-attachment counter for both read and draw targets, or explicitly map each texture attachment to its actual color attachment index.

column5: The integration test depends on a production default to create its gRPC collector bean. An explicit test property makes the fixture self-contained.
column7: Removing the explicit `zipkin.collector.grpc.enabled=true` makes this integration test implicitly rely on the production default from `@ConditionalOnProperty(..., matchIfMissing = true)`. If that default is changed, or if the property is overridden in the test environment, the gRPC collector bean will not be created and this test will either fail to start or stop exercising the intended endpoint. Keeping the property in the test makes the fixture self-contained and resilient to future configuration changes.

column5: The process count is an unreliable launch-context heuristic, and the unchecked WinAPI failure can be mistaken for valid data. The review asks for robust detection.
column7: This heuristic is not robust enough to identify a double-click launch. `GetConsoleProcessList` reports attached console processes, not whether the executable was launched from Explorer versus an existing console, and the code does not check the API call for failure. As a result, the branch can misfire or miss the intended case on valid Windows setups with console attachment/redirected stdio variations, and it can also treat an API failure like a normal return value. Recommend checking the WinAPI result and using a more reliable launch-context test (or avoiding this heuristic entirely) before exiting.

column5: An unset resource identity passes null and silently exports every resource. The requested fix gives the filter an explicit default or requires a value.
column7: `getPromFetchIdentify()` returns the raw config value, which is `null` when unset. In `MetricsReader.readMetricsByEndTime(...)`, a `null` identity means all resources are exported, so this collector silently broadens the scrape scope instead of filtering to the intended resource. That is a correctness issue for multi-resource apps and makes the exporter configuration behave differently depending on whether the property is present. Provide an explicit default or fail fast when the identity is required.

column5: The checkpoint flow couples module and optimizer recovery to different reader choices for the same format. The main proposal is one reader/writer abstraction across both paths.
column7: The new PyTorch>=2.3 load path also switches to implicit reader inference only for the module state, while optimizer recovery still hardcodes FileSystemReader below. This creates a mixed loading strategy inside the same checkpoint format, so any checkpoint produced/consumed through the new code path must remain compatible with both the inferred module reader and the explicit optimizer reader. That is an unnecessary compatibility assumption and can break if torch changes the inferred reader semantics independently of FileSystemReader. Please use a single explicit reader/writer abstraction for the entire sharded checkpoint flow or add a compatibility test covering save/load round-trips for both model and optimizer states.

column5: The Rx bulk release reports zero even after a successful release because the underlying implementation returns a constant. The fix propagates the actual count.
column7: The new Rx bulk-release API is inconsistent with the underlying implementation: `RedissonPermitExpirableSemaphore.tryRelease(List<String>)` returns a hardcoded `0`, so any Rx proxy call to `tryRelease(List<String>)` will always complete with `0` even when permits were actually released. This makes the added API unusable for callers that rely on the returned release count and silently masks successful releases as failures. The implementation should delegate to `tryReleaseAsync(List<String>)` (or otherwise compute the actual released count) instead of returning a constant.

column5: Publishing before admin assignment can leave a committed application without its requested admins after a failure. The review requests atomic or failure-safe ordering.
column7: Publishing the creation event before assigning the requested admins creates a failure window: any exception in an `AppCreationEvent` listener, or any downstream failure before the permission call completes, leaves the app committed with no admin assignment from this method. Since `createAppInLocal` is already transactional and persists the app before the event is published, there is no rollback/compensation for a failed event handler. Consider moving the admin assignment into the same transaction before publishing, or explicitly making event handling failure-safe so the requested admins are always applied.

column5: Printing from a low-level helper creates noisy, hard-to-control stdout output. The review requests structured logging or caller-controlled warnings.
column7: Emitting a raw `print()` from a low-level filesystem helper makes cache refreshes noisy on stdout and is hard to suppress in callers or tests. This degrades maintainability and observability, especially because `recursive_search` is used transitively by `get_filename_list_` and cache rebuilds. Prefer structured logging or return the skipped-path information to the caller so the warning policy stays centralized.

column5: A partial scrape failure can leave the checkpoint unchanged, so the next scrape may reread and duplicate the same window. The review asks for safe checkpoint advancement.
column7: The collector advances `lastFetchTime` only in the `nodes == null` branch and after a fully successful scrape. If the scrape throws partway through, the state is not advanced, so the same time window is re-read on the next scrape and can be emitted repeatedly or reprocessed indefinitely under persistent read failures. Update the checkpoint in a `finally`-style path or only after the read boundary has been safely established, so failed scrapes do not cause duplicate exposure.

column5: Validating against a different URL base than the one used to resolve the download can reject legitimate model downloads. The fix uses the same canonical base.
column7: This validation is compared against the unnormalized `about.__download_url__` value, even though the code intentionally constructs `base_url` with a trailing slash before calling `urljoin`. In URL terms, `https://.../download` is not a prefix of the valid result `https://.../download/<filename>`, so a normal filename can be rejected depending on how `urljoin` resolves the path. The check should validate against the normalized `base_url` (or another canonicalized prefix) to avoid blocking legitimate model downloads.

column5: The broad ExtractorError handler hides real form-parsing failures and can silently omit audio. The review asks to handle only the expected missing-form case.
column7: Catching every ExtractorError here is too broad. _form_hidden_inputs raises on any form-lookup/parsing failure, so this change silently masks unexpected HTML/layout regressions and any other extractor error from the form parsing path, then returns no audio instead of surfacing a real extraction problem. That makes failures harder to detect and can hide breakages in InfoQ pages. Prefer narrowing the exception to the specific missing-form case or handling the absence explicitly after a non-throwing lookup.

column5: The new membership branch compares raw list items and ignores the predicate's case-insensitive option. The fix applies the option consistently.
column7: This new branch bypasses the existing case-insensitive handling in `evalStrPredicate`. When `predicate.isIgnoreCase()` is true, `val` and `predicateValue` are normalized before the switch, but `equalsAny(...)` compares against the raw list values using case-sensitive equality. As a result, a rule like `ignoreCase=true` with predicate value `\"Foo,Bar\"` will fail to match an attribute value `\"foo\"`. Recommendation: normalize every list item when `ignoreCase` is enabled, or use a case-insensitive membership helper for `IN`/`NOT_IN`.

column5: The selective-test dependency mapping schedules Lambda tests for unrelated CloudFormation changes. The requested change narrows the test-selection configuration.
column7: This optional-dependency entry makes every CloudFormation change pull in Lambda tests during selective test execution. That is too broad: CloudFormation supports many resource types that do not depend on Lambda, so the mapping will over-select unrelated tests and reduce the effectiveness of test selection. Recommend narrowing this to the specific Lambda-backed CloudFormation features that actually need it, or moving only those feature-specific paths into the test-selection logic instead of a global service-level dependency.

column5: A truthiness check can reject a valid falsy value as though its key were absent. The review asks for explicit presence validation.
column7: This validation rejects any falsy key attribute value, not just a missing attribute. If a caller passes a valid key value that is falsy in Python's truthiness semantics, the code raises a schema error even though the key is present. The check should use explicit presence testing (`is None` / key membership) instead of truthiness so valid inputs are not rejected.

column5: Missing packed scripts or a changed player payload can raise indexing or extraction errors. The review asks to validate those assumptions and handle absent data.
column7: The extraction pipeline assumes the page always contains at least one `eval... </script>` block and that the unpacked payload always contains a `player.setup({sources:...])` fragment. If either assumption fails, `matches[-1]` raises `IndexError` or the regex/search step throws an extractor error, making the extractor brittle for minor site markup changes or pages with multiple/no packed scripts. Add explicit validation and more tolerant parsing, with a fallback error message when the expected script block is absent.

column5: A nonempty-response assertion can pass even if change-set lookup ignores the stack name. The review requests specific IDs and names in the assertions.
column7: This assertion only checks that the API returns any non-empty response. It does not verify that the response corresponds to the recreated stack or that `StackName` is used to disambiguate against similarly named historical stacks. As written, the test would still pass if `describe_change_set` ignored `StackName` and simply returned the change set identified by `ChangeSetName`. Please assert concrete fields such as `ChangeSetId`, `StackId`, and `StackName` against the newly created stack.

column5: The review concerns the Prometheus build-info convention that clients use to infer capabilities from a SkyWalking endpoint. It asks the endpoint to advertise the compatibility it actually provides.
column7: This endpoint exposes a Prometheus-style build-info object with a hardcoded Prometheus version, but the server is SkyWalking/OAP and does not implement Prometheus 2.45 semantics wholesale. Clients such as Grafana may use `/api/v1/status/buildinfo` for capability/version detection; advertising `2.45.0` can make them assume unsupported Prometheus behavior is available, causing incorrect UI/runtime feature selection. Recommend returning an explicit SkyWalking-compatible identifier or documenting/providing a version string that matches the actual supported Prometheus API subset.

column5: The rule indexes a second regex match even though a normal conda error can contain only one. The review requests safe parsing before selecting a match.
column7: This assumes two separate regex matches are always present, but the actual conda error format shown in the repository test fixture only contains one suggestion line (`Did you mean 'conda list'?`). In that common case, `match[1]` raises `IndexError`, so the rule crashes instead of returning a correction. Recommend parsing the broken command and the suggested command explicitly from the error text, or validating the match count before indexing.

column5: The selector can choose an advertised hash algorithm that the hashing path cannot execute, causing archive validation to fail even when a usable option exists.
column7: The fallback path iterates every non-prioritised algorithm exposed by hashlib, but that set is not limited to safe, one-shot digest algorithms. If a package advertises an algorithm that is present in `hashlib.algorithms_available` but is not suitable for `get_file_hash` in this code path, the helper can return it and cause archive validation to fail later even though a usable digest may also be available. The selection should be restricted to algorithms known to work with the hashing implementation, or the helper should explicitly filter to the same supported subset used elsewhere.

column5: Rebuilding optimizer state from unchecked files silently accepts missing or extra shards and leaves inconsistent state. The review calls for expected-key validation.
column7: Clearing `optim_fragment` and then rebuilding it from an unchecked directory listing means any missing or extra optimizer-state files are silently accepted. Since `get_optim_state_fragment()` and `get_optim_state_keys()` depend on this map, a partially populated or polluted directory will leave the object in an inconsistent state without an explicit validation error. Restore explicit expected-key validation so the loader fails fast when the checkpoint set is incomplete or contains unexpected files.

column3: Cloned, Deprecated, Unneeded, and Commented-out Code
column5: The helper has no callers, and the review explicitly proposes removing it. Its invalid instance-method signature also prevents straightforward reuse.
column7: This method is defined with the wrong signature for an `InfoExtractor` helper: it is missing `self` and `url`, and it is never used. As written, any future call like `self._generic_title(url)` will fail with a `TypeError`, and the dead method adds confusion. Either remove it or implement the standard `_generic_title(self, url)` override correctly.

column5: Lowercasing the cache key without aligning the storage lookup can make valid release messages invisible and repeatedly cache an empty result.
column7: When the ignore-case mode is enabled, the cache key is normalized to lowercase before loading, but the loader still queries `releaseMessageService.findLatestReleaseMessageForMessages(Lists.newArrayList(key))` using that normalized cache key as the only message identifier. If the underlying release-message storage or publisher uses a different canonical case than the lowercased form expected by this feature, the cache will repeatedly load a `nullConfigCacheEntry` and never recover. Please normalize the lookup consistently at the release-message layer or ensure the loader accepts both casings.

column5: The OpenAPI creation path omits the app-master role assignments that initialize admin access in the portal flow. The requested change addresses authorization setup for new applications.
column7: The OpenAPI local-create path does not replicate the portal create flow that assigns app-master roles to the supplied admins. As written, the new endpoint publishes the creation event but leaves the app without the expected admin-role initialization, which changes authorization behavior after creation. Please either accept/administer admins in the OpenAPI payload and assign them here, or explicitly document that OpenAPI-created apps are created without admin binding and add a follow-up initialization step.

column5: A truthiness test treats an explicit zero width as omitted and applies different scaling. The requested fix distinguishes zero from None.
column7: This condition treats `width=0.0` (and other falsy numeric values) as if no width was supplied, so the object is scaled by `unit_size` instead of honoring the explicit width parameter. The previous implementation used `if self.width:`, which also had this problem, but the new API now exposes `width` as a formal constructor argument and should distinguish `None` from numeric zero. Recommend changing the branch to `if width is not None:` so valid numeric widths are handled consistently.

column5: The comment field is blank, so it contains no review intent covered by the taxonomy. No Review Content identifies an empty record without inferring a finding.
A delayed first scrape can calculate a start time after its end time and skip the initial metric batch. The review asks for a safe cursor or a bounds check.
column7: The first scrape can query an invalid interval. `lastFetchTime` is initialized to the current second, while `endTime` is reduced by the configured delay; when `delayTime > 0` (or simply before enough time has elapsed), `beginTimeMs` is greater than `endTimeMs`. `MetricSearcher.findByTimeAndResource(...)` is not documented or implemented to handle reversed bounds, so this can skip the intended first batch of metrics and break incremental collection semantics. Initialize the first fetch cursor to an earlier safe lower bound or guard against `beginTimeMs > endTimeMs` before querying.

column5: The parser imposes stricter duration-component rules and rejects input the previous implementation and tests accepted. The review asks to preserve or explicitly specify that compatibility change.
column7: The new parser rejects strings like `12:34:56:65`, even though the existing tests and prior implementation accepted them and interpreted the fields as integers without range restriction. Since the docstring/API only says `DD:HH:MM:SS`, this regex now enforces exactly two digits for hours/minutes/seconds and will also reject otherwise plausible inputs such as `0:1:2:3` or any duration with values outside two digits per component. This is a backwards-incompatible behavior change for inputs previously accepted. Recommendation: either preserve the old permissive integer parsing or clearly document and test the stricter format if it is intended.

column5: Comparing exception objects does not verify that the original exception is unreachable through the returned cause or context chain. The review asks for direct chain assertions.
column7: This assertion is too weak to verify the stated behavior. `skip_exceptions()` returns a copied exception object, so `root_exception != skipped_exception` can pass even if the original exception is still attached via `__cause__` or `__context__`. That means a regression that continues to retain the original exception chain would not be caught. The test should assert on identity/chain relationships directly, e.g. that `skipped_exception.__cause__` is not the root exception and that the original exception is not reachable through the returned exception chain.

column5: The new rejection of encoding=None in follow propagates through the existing follow_all API, even though that API still accepts the argument. The review asks to preserve or align the public contract.
column7: Response.follow_all still accepts an Optional[str] encoding parameter and forwards it to follow() for each URL, but Response.follow now rejects encoding=None. That makes follow_all inconsistent with the TextResponse override (which normalizes None) and means any caller using Response.follow_all(..., encoding=None) will get a runtime ValueError from the first yielded request. If None is meant to be unsupported, the parameter type/default and documentation should be tightened; otherwise follow_all should normalize None before delegating.

column5: Indexing the first source assumes it exists and is the correct playlist. The review asks to select a valid HLS source defensively and handle missing data.
column7: This assumes the API always returns a non-empty `sources` array and that the first element is the desired playlist. If FlexTV returns an empty list, a different schema, or multiple sources ordered differently, extraction will fail with `IndexError`/`KeyError` or pick the wrong stream. Use defensive traversal/selection (for example `traverse_obj` with an explicit HLS filter or a clear fallback) and raise a user-facing extractor error when no valid source exists.

column5: Asynchronous deletes bypass configured retries and fail immediately on transient errors. The requested fix makes the retry wrapper cover deletion.
column7: Async delete operations bypass the new retry mechanism entirely. Since `MapOptions.writerAsync(...)` now always wraps the writer in `RetryableMapWriterAsync`, callers will expect the configured retry attempts/interval to apply uniformly, but `delete()` still delegates directly and will fail fast on transient writer errors. This can leave write-behind delete operations unretried while insert/update operations retry, creating inconsistent durability behavior. Recommendation: implement the same retry loop for `delete()` or document explicitly that retry settings only apply to writes, not deletes.

column5: A size check can pass after a fallback downloader runs. The review requests an assertion or mock that verifies actual aria2p backend selection.
column7: The test only validates that a file of the expected size appears, not that `external_downloader='aria2p'` actually selected the aria2p backend. Given the downloader selection code can fall back to other downloaders when the external one is unavailable or rejected, this can produce false positives. Add an assertion that the aria2p downloader was actually used or mock the downloader selection/RPC layer so the test verifies the intended code path.

column5: Greedy heading extraction can return HTML, and a colon delimiter can truncate valid series names. Both issues can yield incorrect video metadata.
column7: Both regexes are fragile and can over-capture HTML. `(?si)(.*)` is greedy across any nested markup and can return raw HTML or unintended content if the heading contains tags or multiple lines. Similarly, the `` pattern stops at the first colon, which truncates legitimate series names containing colons. This can produce incorrect metadata even when the video download succeeds. Use a safer HTML title extraction helper or a non-greedy, HTML-aware pattern, and avoid assuming colons delimit the series name.

column5: Unvalidated hash entries can yield invalid algorithm tokens and fail archive verification despite an available digest. The review asks to validate the entry format and algorithm.
column7: The validation now depends on `get_highest_priority_hash_type(...)` choosing a supported algorithm, but the code derives `hash_types` by blindly splitting on `\":\"` and then accepts any fallback algorithm from `hashlib.algorithms_available`. That makes archive validation brittle for future or malformed lockfile entries whose hash names contain additional colons or nonstandard encoding, because the algorithm extraction can be wrong and validation will fail even when a matching digest is present. Use a parser that only accepts the exact `algorithm:hexdigest` shape and validate the algorithm token explicitly before computing the digest.

column5: The comment field is blank, so it contains no review intent covered by the taxonomy. No Review Content identifies an empty record without inferring a finding.
Optimized Python removes the assertion and its required interval bookkeeping. The fix records coverage unconditionally so later reads see the prefetched range.
column7: This path relies on `minimal_intervals_covering()` as a side effect to mark the prefetched tail chunk as already downloaded, but it uses the result only inside an `assert`. In optimized Python runs (`-O`), the assertion is removed and the bookkeeping update is skipped entirely, so the tail chunk is not recorded as covered and later reads can re-download overlapping ranges or mis-handle interval merging. The code should perform the bookkeeping unconditionally, not inside an assertion.

column5: The cleaner executor is never shut down and can leave its worker blocked or alive during teardown. The review requests explicit executor shutdown and interruption handling.
column7: The background cleaner thread is created with a long-lived executor, but shutdown only sets a flag. If the queue is empty, the worker can stay blocked/sleeping for up to a minute before it observes the flag, and the executor is never shut down or interrupted. This can delay application shutdown and leave a non-daemon thread running. Recommend explicitly calling `shutdownNow()`/`shutdown()` on the executor in `@PreDestroy` and handling interruption in the loop.

column5: The fallback returns default painting for valid blend modes that lack a switch case. The review asks to apply the correct platform mapping or handle the fallback explicitly.
column7: This fallback drops every blend mode not explicitly handled in the non-Q switch, including MULTIPLY and the other newly added modes. Since FillContent.draw() consumes this method directly, those layers will render with the default paint blend mode instead of the parsed Lottie blend mode. The converter should either invoke the Q+ mapping when the runtime supports it or provide a complete fallback mapping strategy so unsupported modes are not silently ignored.

column5: A previously nonfatal node-count heuristic becomes a mandatory divisibility check that rejects distributed jobs the old detection path tolerated.
column7: This makes distributed environment detection fail for any initialized CUDA-based distributed job where `world_size` is not an exact multiple of the number of visible GPUs. That includes valid topologies such as heterogeneous multi-node jobs (different GPU counts per node), CPU-only distributed jobs launched with a CUDA build, or cases where `world_size` is intentionally unrelated to `torch.cuda.device_count()`. The previous logic only derived `num_nodes` when CUDA was available and did not hard-fail; this change turns a heuristic into a global runtime exception. Recommendation: avoid enforcing a CUDA divisibility invariant in environment detection; compute `num_nodes` only when the mapping is known from launcher/configuration, or make the validation optional and limited to GPU strategies that truly require it.

column5: An H2 bootstrap error can propagate through bean creation and prevent application startup. The review requests handling appropriate to the startup policy.
column7: This initialization hook now runs during bean creation and propagates any checked/unchecked failure as a startup failure. If the H2 script is malformed, missing, or the DataSource is temporarily unavailable, the entire BizDBPropertySource bean will fail to initialize and can prevent the application context from starting. Consider making this initialization best-effort for the H2 test profile only, and log/handle failures explicitly if startup availability is more important than aborting the service.

column5: The timeout fallback discards the requested model ID and can route requests away from replicas with the model loaded. The requested fix preserves model affinity during fallback.
column7: After the multiplexed-model timeout expires, the scheduler stops considering the requested model ID entirely and falls back to every replica in the deployment. That means a request that was explicitly intended for a multiplexed model can be routed to a replica that does not have the model loaded, defeating multiplexing and potentially causing avoidable cold starts or incorrect model affinity. The fallback should still prefer replicas that can serve the requested model, or the timeout path should be constrained so it does not broaden to unrelated replicas.

column5: Strict service loading does not expand the optional service dependencies advertised by the new map. The requested fix aligns dependency resolution and configuration semantics.
column7: The new optional dependency map is not used by the strict service-loading path. `resolve_apis()` in `localstack/utils/bootstrap.py` still expands only `API_DEPENDENCIES`, and `get_enabled_apis()` delegates to that function. As a result, allow-listing a service via `SERVICES`/strict loading will not automatically enable documented optional companions like `logs` for `lambda` or `sqs`/`firehose` for `sns`, even though those features depend on them. This can leave a service partially functional or fail at runtime when an optional integration is exercised. Recommendation: either merge optional dependencies into strict loading as well, or clearly separate the data structures so the documentation does not imply runtime loading support that does not exist.

column5: An update-site URL without the expected suffix can send SetupWizard to the wrong endpoint. The review asks for robust URL derivation or a validated fallback.
column7: This derivation is overly brittle: it assumes every update-site URL literally contains \"/update-center.json\" and otherwise leaves the URL unchanged. If an administrator configures a nonstandard update site URL or a URL variant that does not match this exact substring, SetupWizard will use the wrong endpoint and fail to load suggested plugins. Please compute the new URL from the parsed base path or validate the expected suffix and report an error/fallback when it is not present.

column5: The framebuffer validation rejects valid multisampling configurations containing non-color texture attachments. The review asks to narrow the rejection to unsupported cases.
column7: This rejects multisampled framebuffers whenever any texture attachment is present, including the common and valuable case of a multisampled color renderbuffer plus depth/stencil textures or other non-color textures. The later transfer() logic already tries to resolve only color attachments, so the validation is broader than necessary and blocks legitimate configurations. Recommend narrowing the check to disallow only multisampled color texture attachments, or implementing support for resolving texture-backed attachments explicitly.

column5: The role check reads unfinished futures and can treat an existing master as absent. The requested fix waits for asynchronous role checks before deciding.
column7: This checks `roles` immediately after starting the async work, but it never waits for the futures to complete before reading them with `getNow(...)`. As a result, a slow or still-running check can be treated as `slave`, causing the code to conclude that no master exists even when a master is present. That can incorrectly start the unreachable timer or even throw `RedisConnectionException` after the timeout. The implementation should await completion of the node checks before evaluating the set of roles.

column5: The HTTP Basic filter enables broad authentication without a defined credential source or explicit request authorization policy. The review asks to configure or scope access controls.
column7: This introduces HTTP Basic security for the `assembly` profile without any authorization rules or user/credential setup in the adminservice module. In practice, that means the security filter chain becomes globally active and defaults to requiring authentication for all requests, but the module does not show where valid users are provisioned. In the all-in-one `apollo-assembly` launch, this can make the admin service inaccessible unless additional, undocumented credentials are supplied elsewhere. Please add explicit request authorization plus a concrete authentication source, or scope the security config to the intended endpoints only.

column5: The truncation branch assigns failed-domain data to the renewed-domain variable, leaving one value untruncated and overwriting the other.
column7: The truncation branch writes the failed-domain slice into `renewed_domains_str` instead of `failed_domains_str`. As a result, `FAILED_DOMAINS` remains untruncated and `RENEWED_DOMAINS` is accidentally overwritten with failed-domain data. This should assign to `failed_domains_str`.

column5: Malformed or wrongly typed JSON can propagate an exception or unusable retention settings. The review asks for validation and a default fallback.
column7: The new config accessor parses an arbitrary string with `GSON.fromJson(...)` and does not catch parse/type errors or validate the result. If the DB-backed property contains malformed JSON, an empty object where a map is expected, or values that are not integers, this method can throw at runtime or return an unusable result, which then breaks `ReleaseHistoryService.getReleaseHistoryRetentionLimit()` during release creation/cleanup. Please harden this path by validating the JSON and falling back to an empty map or the default retention size on parse failure.

column5: A page with no matching HTML5 media makes entries[0] raise IndexError. The requested guard reports a controlled extraction failure.
column7: This assumes the page always contains at least one HTML5 media entry. If pr0gramm changes markup, serves an age/login/interstitial page, or the extractor’s regex fails to match the video tag, `entries` will be empty and `entries[0]` will raise `IndexError` instead of a clean extraction failure. Use a guarded check and raise `ExtractorError`/`expected=True` when no media entry is found.

column5: Reading the same reflected field twice omits the lazy-concrete serializer set and can route values to the wrong codec.
column7: The blacklist initialization reads from the wrong reflected field on the second addAll call: it still uses concreteField instead of _concreteLazyField. This silently drops the entire lazy-concrete serializer set from CLASSES_NOT_SUITABLE_FOR_PROTOBUF, so classes that should be routed away from protobuf may be encoded with the wrong format. Please read from _concreteLazyField when populating that set.

column5: The review asks to move dashboard-specific import-path policy into the job configuration layer so that its responsibility is explicit. It also proposes a regression test for the resulting policy.
column7: This new namespace check suppresses only the script directory, but dashboard jobs are started through an internal `ray.init(..., namespace=RAY_INTERNAL_DASHBOARD_NAMESPACE)` path and may not have a meaningful `driver_name`/script origin at all. The code still relies on `sys.path` membership for the script directory and then unconditionally appends the current working directory, so dashboard execution can diverge from normal driver behavior in a way that is hard to reason about and is not covered by a compensating path elsewhere in the repository. Recommend making the dashboard rule explicit at the job-config layer and adding a regression test for dashboard-launched handlers to pin the expected import path behavior.

column5: Reusing a mutated frame across calls can leak old argument bindings into later invocations. The review asks for isolated or restored per-call state.
column7: This function mutates `global_stack[0]` in place for every invocation, but never snapshots or restores it afterward. Because `global_stack[0]` is reused across calls, any previously bound parameters or keyword arguments can remain visible on later calls when those arguments are omitted. That creates state leakage between independent invocations of the same JS function closure and can produce wrong results for functions that depend on argument absence/default-like behavior. The fix is to create a fresh per-call locals dict (or save/restore the frame) before updating it.

column5: Calling total_seconds on an absent or differently represented ETA can abort an otherwise active transfer. The review asks for guarded access.
column7: This code assumes `download.eta` is always a timedelta-like object with `total_seconds()`, but aria2p can expose missing/unknown ETA as `None` or another non-timedelta representation depending on state and version. In such cases this line raises an exception and aborts the download loop even though the transfer is still in progress. Recommendation: guard the ETA access and fall back to `None` when the value is unavailable.

column5: The comment field is blank, so it contains no review intent covered by the taxonomy. No Review Content identifies an empty record without inferring a finding.
Building a batched shape and slicing it for unbatched symbolic inputs can infer the wrong output shape. The review asks to branch on rank first.
column7: The symbolic output-shape logic is fragile for rank-3 inputs because it unconditionally builds a 4D shape first and only then slices off the batch dimension. This couples unbatched and batched shape inference in a way that can mis-handle symbolic shapes and makes the rank-3 path depend on the presence of a first dimension that does not exist for unbatched images. The implementation should branch on rank before constructing the output shape, mirroring the explicit handling used elsewhere in the file.

column5: The new nested-container guard may reject a flat sequence accepted by the existing unflatten_as contract when optree classifies it differently. The review asks to preserve flat-sequence acceptance.
column7: This guard rejects any `flat_sequence` that `is_nested()` does not classify as nested. That is too restrictive for `unflatten_as`, whose contract is to unpack a flat sequence into a structure and whose own test suite uses plain Python lists such as `tree.unflatten_as(None, [1])`. If optree ever classifies a valid flat container differently from the old tree implementation, valid callers will now fail with `TypeError`. Recommendation: validate only that `flat_sequence` is a finite sequence-like container of the right arity, rather than requiring it to be “nested”.

column5: An unavailable aria2p backend can remain selectable even though its module name is unbound. The review asks to make availability checks consistent with selection.
column7: The availability check only records a boolean at class-definition time, but the actual downloader later assumes the module name `aria2p` is always bound. In this code path, if the package is absent the class remains present in the registry yet `_call_downloader` will fail before any network activity. This makes the backend fragile and harder to reason about; the module import should be handled once at module scope or the downloader should be hidden from selection entirely when unavailable.

column5: The shared test crawler factory loses its default warning suppression, affecting test setup across the suite. The review asks to restore or explicitly migrate that fixture behavior.
column7: This removes the helper’s only warning-suppression behavior. `get_crawler()` is used extensively throughout the test suite, and without setting `REQUEST_FINGERPRINTER_IMPLEMENTATION` to the legacy value, `RequestFingerprinter.__init__()` will emit `ScrapyDeprecationWarning` during crawler setup. That is a functional regression for any test or caller relying on the default `prevent_warnings=True` contract. Restore the setting assignment or update the helper/API and all callers accordingly.

column5: The symbolic inverse-error-function path dispatches to the ordinary error function, so graph-mode inputs compute the wrong operation.
column7: Symbolic tensors are dispatched to `Erf().symbolic_call(x)` instead of the newly added `ErfInv` operation. That means `keras.ops.erfinv()` will compute `erf(x)` for symbolic inputs, producing the wrong function in graph mode. Please change this branch to `ErfInv().symbolic_call(x)`.

column5: The comment field is blank, so it contains no review intent covered by the taxonomy. No Review Content identifies an empty record without inferring a finding.
The public converter never reaches the Android Q mapping, so supported blend modes render incorrectly. The primary remedy is to wire the mapping into runtime dispatch.
column7: The Q-only mapper is dead code: static inspection shows no call site for toNativeBlendModeQ(), and the public toNativeBlendMode() method never delegates to it. As a result, all Q-supported blend modes added in this enum remain unreachable and are always treated as null. This defeats the purpose of introducing the enum values and causes incorrect rendering on Android 10+ as well. Wire the public API to the Q helper behind an SDK check, or remove the unused helper and clearly handle unsupported modes elsewhere.

column5: The restrictive Next.js data capture can miss a valid page payload and abort extraction. The review asks for a more tolerant parser.
column7: The `__NEXT_DATA__` parser is too restrictive: it only matches a single `[^<]+` chunk, which is brittle for script contents that contain newlines or other formatting changes. Other extractors in this codebase use a more tolerant JSON capture pattern for Next.js data, so this implementation can fail to parse a valid Callin page and abort extraction. Use a broader, multiline-safe capture pattern consistent with the existing Next.js extractors.

column5: The rule assumes two ordered command matches, so shorter or localized error output can make it crash. The review requests separate parsing and bounds checks.
column7: This code assumes the stderr always contains at least two quoted `conda ...` tokens and that they appear in a fixed order. If the help text changes, is localized, or only emits the suggested command without the original mistyped command, `match[1]` will raise `IndexError` and the rule will crash instead of being safely ignored. Please parse the command and suggestion separately and guard against missing matches before indexing.

column5: Setting retry options after the async writer leaves the writer unwrapped despite the final configuration. The review asks to resolve the wrapper independently of setter order.
column7: The async writer has the same order-dependency bug as the synchronous one: retries are only enabled if `writerRetryAttempts(...)` has already been set before `writerAsync(...)` is called. Any later retry configuration leaves `writerAsync` unwrapped, so the retry feature is not applied even though the final options object contains retry settings. Rebuild or lazily resolve the wrapper after all options are configured.

column5: The comment field is blank, so it contains no review intent covered by the taxonomy. No Review Content identifies an empty record without inferring a finding.
Writing each response at the same start offset can overwrite previously fetched disjoint ranges and corrupt the wheel. The fix seeks to the offset of each range.
column7: The file pointer is reset to `start` for every fetched sub-range, not to `range_start`. If `minimal_intervals_covering()` yields more than one disjoint interval in a single call, each HTTP response is written at the same offset and overwrites the previous data instead of filling the requested span. This corrupts the temporary wheel and can make later ZIP reads fail or return wrong metadata. The write position should follow each interval (`self.seek(range_start)`) before writing that chunk.

column5: Returning null for NORMAL and HARD_MIX can silently ignore a declared compositing mode. The review asks for explicit mapping or unsupported-mode handling.
column7: Two declared blend modes are effectively unimplemented: `NORMAL` and `HARD_MIX` both return `null`, so the renderer silently falls back to the paint's existing blend mode instead of honoring the composition's requested mode. This means valid JSON values are ignored at runtime, producing incorrect rendering with no warning. Map these cases explicitly (or reject them with a warning) so the behavior is deterministic.

column5: The fallback still returns no title when a renderer supplies neither of the assumed fields. The review asks to account for renderer-specific metadata.
column7: The new `headline.simpleText` fallback is only safe if `headline` is present on all renderer types that reach `_extract_video`, but the extractor still processes many non-Shorts renderers through the same path. If a renderer lacks both `title` and `headline`, the fallback does not help and the code will continue to return `None`, producing entries with missing titles. Consider normalizing title extraction per renderer type or adding a dedicated Shorts renderer handler before calling `_extract_video`.

column5: A minimum count of zero lets an empty playlist pass the regression test. The review requests a meaningful bound or stronger entry assertions.
column7: Lowering the playlist minimum count to 0 removes the test's ability to catch regressions where the group extractor stops returning entries entirely. Since this fixture previously expected hundreds of items, the assertion no longer enforces that the pagination/extraction logic is functioning. Please keep a meaningful lower bound or replace it with a stronger assertion on extracted entries.

column5: Mapping all lead-present cases to the same ObjGap value loses actual distance information and can send the wrong dash or ACC signal.
column7: This change hard-codes `ObjGap` to only two states and ignores the actual distance-based meanings documented in the comment. By collapsing all lead-present cases to `2`, the dash/ACC object-gap signal will no longer reflect the true lead distance, which degrades visual fidelity and may diverge from vehicle expectations. Please map this field from a real distance/spacing metric instead of a boolean lead flag.

column5: A direct media download can be handed to the HLS parser as if it were a manifest. The review requests type validation or fallback to a known playlist field.
column7: The new precedence change assumes `links.download` is always an HLS playlist, but the code does not validate its type before handing it to the m3u8 parser. If the API returns a direct MP4 download URL or any non-manifest link in `links.download`, extraction will fail at manifest parsing time. Please gate this value with a manifest-specific check or fall back to the known HLS URL field when the download link is not an `.m3u8` resource.

column5: The URL pattern can claim unrelated FileMoon paths and treat arbitrary trailing segments as titles. The review asks for precise matching and a stable title source.
column7: The URL matcher is too broad and fragile. `./` accepts any single path character, so the extractor will match many URLs beyond the intended `/e/` or equivalent embed path, and it also treats any trailing path segment as `title`. This can misclassify unrelated FileMoon pages and produce incorrect titles for valid video URLs that include extra path components. Tighten the regex to the exact supported path shape and derive the title from a stable source or leave it unset unless explicitly needed.

column5: The test may change the table configuration while the procedure reads a separate merged snapshot. The review asks to verify the setup or assert against the effective configuration.
column7: The test assumes a config update on `tableEnv.getConfig()` is reflected in the execution environment used by the procedure call. The procedure implementation reads `ProcedureContext.getExecutionEnvironment().getConfiguration()`, and the production call path constructs that environment from a merged `Configuration` snapshot. If the table environment caches or reuses the execution environment across calls, the updated table config may not be visible, making this test flaky or misleading. Please verify the environment is rebuilt per call or assert against the actual merged config source directly.

column5: Shell-style tokenization changes the tag lists returned for existing metadata with quotes or commas. The review explicitly asks to preserve the previous parsing semantics or define the source format.
column7: This fallback changes tag parsing from simple whitespace splitting to shell-style tokenization, which is not equivalent for YouTube metadata. `keywords` commonly contains human-authored strings where commas are separators and quotes are literal or inconsistently balanced; `shlex.split` will merge quoted phrases and can also raise parsing differences from the previous behavior. That means the extractor can now emit a different tag list for existing channels/playlist metadata, especially where commas or embedded quotes are present. A safer approach is to keep the previous splitting semantics or explicitly parse the exact delimiter format used by the source field, with regression tests for comma/quote-containing keywords.

column5: A null time unit causes a dereference during conversion. The review asks to reject it explicitly at the API boundary.
column7: `timeUnit` is not validated. Passing `null` will fail with a `NullPointerException` inside `timeUnit.toMillis(...)`, which is a poor API contract and makes misconfiguration harder to diagnose. Recommendation: explicitly reject `null` with `Objects.requireNonNull(timeUnit, \"timeUnit\")` or a clear `IllegalArgumentException` before conversion.

column5: Starting the maximum at zero produces a false maximum when every input is negative. The review asks for a seed valid across the long domain.
column7: The max accumulator starts at Java's default `0`, which is incorrect for this reducer. If all accepted values are negative, `accept()` and `combine()` will never update the field because each input is less than `0`, so the stored maximum becomes `0` instead of the true negative maximum. Initialize the field to `Long.MIN_VALUE` (or otherwise seed it on first input) so max works for the full `long` domain.

column5: The integration test shuts down a shared Spring-managed server, which can affect other tests or teardown. The review requests an isolated context or lifecycle hook.
column7: Closing the autowired `Server` directly inside the integration test mutates the Spring-managed application context under test. That can leak shutdown side effects into the test framework's own lifecycle and makes the class fragile if any later test, listener, or teardown code expects the server bean to still be alive. A safer pattern is to exercise deregistration through a dedicated lifecycle hook or isolated test context rather than shutting down the shared bean in-place.

column5: The extractor embeds one fixed Origin despite supporting several sites. The review asks to derive that request value from the matched host.
column7: The new season extractor handles multiple hostnames and show paths, but it still sends every Algolia request with a fixed `Origin` of `https://www.americastestkitchen.com`. For `cookscountry.com` and `cooksillustrated.com` URLs this makes the request origin inconsistent with the matched site, which can break origin validation, caching, or site-specific response shaping. The request should derive the origin from the matched host rather than hardcoding ATK.

column5: Reset leaves the previous restriction stored on the object, allowing stale state when the axis is reused or inspected. The review requests a complete state reset.
column7: This reset only disables the flag but leaves the previous restriction value stored on the object. That means the feature state is not fully reset, which is surprising for a reset API and can produce stale behavior if the axis state is later reused or inspected. Clear the stored restriction value as well, or make the reset contract explicit and add tests covering repeated enable/disable cycles.

column5: A playlist item without canonical links can trigger an exception and abort extraction. The review asks to skip incomplete items safely.
column7: This playlist walker now filters `data['data']` by requiring `v['canonical_links']['self']` during traversal, but still assumes each yielded item is the full episode dict. If RoosterTeeth returns a season/bonus-feature record without `canonical_links` (or with a different shape for a subset of items), the lambda will raise and abort the entire playlist extraction instead of skipping the bad record. The previous implementation iterated over the JSON array directly and was less brittle. Recommend traversing the list with a safe predicate and guarding access to `canonical_links` via `traverse_obj(..., 'canonical_links', 'self')` or a defaulted lookup before emitting each entry.

column5: The wording misstates when the checkpoint directory is used. The requested change documents the distinction between default storage selection and explicit jobmanager configuration.
column7: This wording is misleading because `state.checkpoints.dir` is not generally a persistence target for `jobmanager` checkpoint storage in the sense implied here; in the codebase it is primarily an externalized checkpoint/savepoint location, and the loader only falls back to `CHECKPOINTS_DIRECTORY` when checkpoint storage itself is unspecified. Please tighten the documentation to describe the exact loader behavior and the distinction between default selection and explicit `jobmanager` configuration.

column5: A role-assignment failure can leave the app created without the requested role and violate the promised atomic operation. The proposed service-level transaction addresses partial failure.
column7: The endpoint performs creation and optional role assignment in two separate service calls, but it only guards the method with `@Transactional` at the controller layer. In this codebase, the actual creation path publishes events and performs repository writes in `AppService.createAppAndAddRolePermission(...)`; the new controller bypasses that established flow and directly calls `appOpenApiService.createApp(req)`, then assigns the role afterward. If role assignment fails after the app has been created, the controller-level transaction does not guarantee that all downstream side effects from the creation path are rolled back consistently, because the creation service may emit events or execute actions outside the controller's direct control. This can leave the system with a created app but without the requested consumer role, which breaks the advertised atomic behavior of \"create and assign to self\". Recommendation: move the create-and-assign orchestration into a single service method that owns the transaction and performs both steps atomically, or make the OpenAPI service itself handle the combined operation.

column5: Missing ORC value-count statistics can abort an otherwise readable aggregation query. The review asks for a fallback when pushdown cannot use those statistics.
column7: COUNT(column) pushdown now depends on `columnStatistics.hasNumberOfValues()` for every ORC file. If the ORC footer does not store `numberOfValues` for that column, `writeNonNullCount()` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`, so an otherwise readable file can no longer satisfy a partial-aggregation query. This is a regression in robustness for the new ORC aggregated path. Recommend either falling back to a non-pushed-down read when value-count statistics are absent, or aligning the behavior with other readers by handling the missing-statistics case without aborting the query.

column5: The downloader can misclassify terminal outcomes and leave progress stale. The review asks to use the documented success condition and emit final status.
column7: The downloader exits the polling loop and returns failure for any terminal state other than exactly `complete`, but aria2p/aria2 can legitimately finish in other non-active states such as canceled/error/removed. More importantly, the loop never emits a final progress update after completion, so the last reported state may be stale and the method can misclassify a successful transfer if the library uses a different success terminal state or if the final status is observed only after the loop. Recommendation: explicitly handle all terminal states from aria2p, emit a final status update, and base success/failure on the API’s documented success condition rather than `!= 'complete'`.
